title: Adobe Acquires Indian AI Startup Rilo in Second India Deal After Rephrase.ai
excerpt: The IIT Bombay-founded marketing automation startup raised $1 million at a $10 million valuation before being acquired less than a year after launch.
body:
• Adobe has acquired Rilo, an Indian AI marketing automation startup founded by IIT Bombay alumni Dhruv Jaglan and Georgi Boby, in a licensing and team acquisition deal less than a year after the company launched.
  • Rilo had raised $1 million from Peak XV Partners, DeVC and Day Zero Ventures at a $10 million valuation and attracted over 10,000 users.
  • The six-member team will join Adobe to integrate agentic AI capabilities into the company's enterprise marketing suite. Rilo's standalone platform will shut down.
  • This marks Adobe's second acquisition of an Indian startup, following its 2023 purchase of AI video platform Rephrase.ai.

Adobe has acquired India-based AI marketing startup Rilo in a deal involving technology licensing and a full team acquisition, TechCrunch reported. The financial terms were not disclosed. Rilo's six-member team, including co-founders Dhruv Jaglan and Georgi Boby, will join Adobe, while the standalone Rilo platform will be shut down.

From IIT Bombay to Adobe

Jaglan and Boby, both IIT Bombay alumni, founded Rilo in September 2025. Jaglan previously built AI recruitment platform Babblebots.ai, while Boby led technology at robotics firm CloudChef, according to Inc42.

https://x.com/bsindia/status/2095360128187089399

Rilo developed an AI-powered workflow automation platform that allowed marketing and go-to-market teams to build complex workflows using natural language instructions. The platform handled competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, social media outreach, LinkedIn prospecting and sales call analysis. Users could create what Rilo described as "AI employees" that executed multi-step tasks across business applications.

The startup scaled to more than 10,000 users within months of launching and raised $1 million in seed funding from Peak XV Partners and DeVC at a reported $10 million valuation.

"Beyond excited to announce that Rilo is joining Adobe to help bring AI to Fortune 500 marketers. This month last year, I started Rilo with Georgi to expand the power of AI to all knowledge workers beyond just engineers."

— Dhruv Jaglan, Co-founder, Rilo

Why It Matters for Adobe

The acquisition bolsters Adobe's push into agentic AI, where software does not just create content but completes multi-step tasks autonomously. Rilo's technology is expected to strengthen automation within Adobe's marketing and customer experience products, particularly for enterprise clients running complex campaigns.

Adobe told Inc42 the deal brings a "strong" technical team into its fold and will enable the company to build broader marketing workflows and integrate Rilo's agentic capabilities into its enterprise suite.

The move comes after Adobe's marquee $1.9 billion acquisition of SEO platform Semrush last year, signaling a sustained investment in AI-driven marketing tools. Rivals including Canva have also expanded their marketing portfolios through acquisitions, while Amazon, Google and Meta have built proprietary AI-powered marketing infrastructure.

India's Growing AI Acquisition Pipeline

Rilo is Adobe's second known acquisition of an Indian startup after it bought generative AI video platform Rephrase.ai in 2023. The deal fits a broader pattern: Mukesh Bansal's Nurix AI announced plans to acquire Verloop.io in July to expand voice AI offerings, SaaS firm MoEngage bought U.S.-based Aampe, and enterprise platform Nitro Commerce acquired Gurugram-based Zodiac Labs AI in March.

According to Inc42's Bharat AI Startups Report 2026, India's AI economy is projected to become a $126 billion opportunity by 2030 and add $1.7 trillion to national GDP by 2035.

"Their workflow builder product was way ahead of the curve and shall be extremely valuable to a giant like Adobe in enhancing customer experience and productivity."

— Rahul Gupta, Managing Partner, Day Zero Ventures

What's Next

Existing Rilo customers will be assisted in transitioning their workflows as the platform is discontinued. For Adobe, the integration of Rilo's technology into its CX and marketing suite could give enterprise clients new tools for handling complex, multi-step marketing workflows at scale.
